svg.title: Property Identification to Documented Case Assessment
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-property-and-genealogy-work-plan; chapter number: 12; title: Property Identification to Documented Case Assessment; subtitle: Check coverage, inspect matches, retrieve evidence, and price the work.; caption: Regrid demonstrators explain coverage and import checks; Seth on REtipster demonstrates ownership and document research; Amy Moyes tests heirship; Vanessa Bland explains the consequences of omitting business expenses.; assumptions note: The week headings are planning slots, not elapsed times reported by Regrid, Seth, Amy Moyes, or Vanessa Bland. Certificates, retrieval, and case resolution may remain outstanding beyond these slots; no four-week completion promise is implied.; note: Regrid states a maximum 30-day sandbox token lifespan and limited trial coverage. Seth reports about 24–48 hours for abstractor document retrieval. Neither establishes an end-to-end heir-recovery timetable.; chart type: timeline_roadmap; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Establish owner identity and coverage; deliverable: Owner-name search and property references, with Regrid trial counties and Seth's title-chain coverage start dates checked.; gate: Do not treat unavailable trial counties or records before the report's start date as evidence of absence.; week: Week 2; title: Inspect parcel matches and owner duplicates; deliverable: Reviewed import matches and a narrowed owner list with duplicate owners removed, following Regrid and Seth.; gate: Inspect match results before Finish Import. Regrid's accepted 97% example is not a universal acceptance threshold.; week: Week 3; title: Retrieve documents and test family assertions; deliverable: Retrieved ownership documents and a family-research record that keeps outstanding certificates visible; divide surname variants among colleagues as Amy Moyes does with Gardner spellings.; gate: Keep the possible-child question tied to certificate evidence. Amy Moyes's cousin interview does not settle whether wider relatives remain entitled.; week: Week 4; title: Assess service pricing and unresolved work; deliverable: Expense-aware genealogy pricing and an assessment that distinguishes signed beneficiaries from unresolved document and entitlement questions.; gate: Apply Vanessa Bland's lesson by including actual business expenses rather than copying an employment wage. Amy Moyes's 18 signed maternal heirs do not replace outstanding evidence.
